report.summary: Analyzed daedalus/lanes/__init__.py chunk 1 of 1. Found no code defects, all public symbols documented, claims about baseline enforcement and design rationale are consistent.

handoff.purpose: Exports and documents the shared lane infrastructure: check baseline, policy, graph brief, reference audit, and judgment functions.

claims.text: A 'lane' is a path by which a model's output becomes a file on disk
claims.why: The docstring defines 'lane'; the code only exports functions and constants. No implementation of a lane is present in this chunk.

claims.text: the baseline lives here, every lane calls run_checks instead of writing its own sequence
claims.why: The chunk exports run_checks but does not show any lane calling it. The claim about lane behavior cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: a lane may ADD checks but may never skip the baseline
claims.why: No lane code or enforcement mechanism is present in this chunk; the claim is about lane contracts not visible here.

claims.text: What deliberately does NOT move here: claims about a specific model.
claims.why: The module exports only generic check and audit functions; no model-specific claims are present.

claims.text: The elision markers are a statement about what one vendor's model emits when it truncates, and two lanes must stay free to disagree about that without silently re-tuning each other's guard.
claims.why: No elision markers or lane-specific tuning logic is present in this chunk. The claim refers to design decisions outside this file.

claims.text: Those arrive as policy; the baseline is shared.
claims.why: The chunk exports BASELINE and BASELINE_POLICY constants, but does not show how policy is applied or how lanes receive it. The claim about policy arrival is outside this chunk.

observations.what: Module docstring describes a historical incident and design rationale, but no executable checks or enforcement code is present in this chunk.
All exported symbols are re-exports from submodules .checks, .graph_brief, and .grounding. No new definitions or logic exist in this file.
